questions.q: What actually distinguishes IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS from each other?
options: How much the service costs per month
Whether the service can be used outside the United States
Where the line is drawn between what Microsoft manages for you and what you manage yourself
How much raw compute power the service provides
questions.explain: The three models aren't about price or power — they're about which layers of the stack Microsoft manages versus which layers you manage.

questions.q: With IaaS, such as an Azure Virtual Machine, who is responsible for patching the operating system?
options: A third-party vendor unrelated to Microsoft or the customer
Nobody — IaaS virtual machines never need OS updates
You are — Microsoft manages the hardware and virtualization, but the OS up is yours
Microsoft always patches the OS automatically with no configuration
questions.explain: IaaS means Microsoft manages the physical datacenter, networking, servers, and virtualization — everything above that, including the OS, is your responsibility.

questions.q: What makes Azure App Service a PaaS example rather than IaaS?
options: It runs on physical hardware you own and rack yourself
It requires you to manually install and patch the web server software
Microsoft manages the operating system and runtime; you only deploy your application code and data
It has no relationship to the concept of service models at all
questions.explain: PaaS extends what IaaS manages to also include the OS and runtime, so you only bring your app and data — no server to patch.

questions.q: Why is Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Word, Teams) an example of SaaS?
options: It's only available as a downloadable installer with no cloud component
It requires you to manage the underlying operating system yourself
Microsoft manages the entire stack, including the application itself — you just use it
It's a service you install and run entirely on your own local server
questions.explain: With SaaS, Microsoft manages everything including the application, so you bring nothing but your own data and configuration.

questions.q: What is the real trade-off you give up as you move from IaaS toward SaaS?
options: Control — you manage less of the stack yourself in exchange for Microsoft handling more of it
Nothing at all — there is no meaningful trade-off between the three models
Security — SaaS applications are inherently less secure than IaaS
Internet access — SaaS applications cannot be reached online
questions.explain: Moving from IaaS to PaaS to SaaS, you manage less and Microsoft manages more, trading control for convenience — that trade-off, not price, is the real decision.
